body: $P = \{1, 2, 3, 8, 10\}$ and $Q = \{8, 1, x, 3, 2\}$. If $P = Q$, what is the value of $x$?

options.hint: Correct. 10 is the member of $P$ missing from $Q$.

hint: Equal sets have exactly the same members.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Every member of $P$ must be in $Q$. Only 10 is not listed in $Q$, so $x = 10$.

## Simplified explanation

Compare the sets. $Q$ has 1, 2, 3 and 8 already. The only one missing is 10.

body: $Y =$ {house, tree} and $V =$ {cat, house, tree}. Which of the following is true of $Y$ and $V$?

options.hint: Correct. Every member of $Y$ is in $V$.
Cat is in $V$ but not in $Y$.
$V$ is a set, not a member of $Y$.

hint: Does every member of one set appear in the other?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Both members of $Y$ are in $V$, and $V$ has an extra member, so $Y$ is a proper subset of $V$.

## Simplified explanation

House and tree are both in $V$, so $Y$ sits inside $V$.

body: The following addition is in base ten. Find the missing addend.

media.caption: Column addition: 2345 plus 1045 plus a missing number gives 5110.

options.hint: This is more than the difference.

hint: Add the two known numbers, then subtract from the total.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$5110 - (2345 + 1045) = 5110 - 3390 = 1720$.

## Simplified explanation

2345 and 1045 add to 3390. Taking that from 5110 leaves 1720.

body: Given that $2^2 \times 3^2 \times 7 = 252$, find the least number that should be multiplied by 252 to make the product a perfect square.
hint: In a perfect square, every prime has an even power.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Only 7 has an odd power, so multiply by 7: $2^2 \times 3^2 \times 7^2 = 42^2$.

## Simplified explanation

$2^2$ and $3^2$ are already squares. The 7 needs a partner, so multiply by 7.

body: Write 4687.02 in standard form.
hint: The first number must be at least 1 and less than 10.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$4687.02 = 4.68702 \times 10^3$.

## Simplified explanation

Move the point 3 places to the left to get 4.68702. So the power of 10 is 3.

body: Convert $11001_{\text{two}}$ to a decimal numeral.
hint: The place values from the right are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$2^4 + 2^3 + 2^0 = 25$.

## Simplified explanation

Add the place values under each 1: $16 + 8 + 1 = 25$.

body: A boy spends $\dfrac{2}{7}$ of his pocket money on transport and $\dfrac{1}{5}$ on sweets. What fraction of his pocket money does he spend on transport and sweets?

options.hint: Use 35 as the denominator, and change both tops.
This adds the tops and bottoms. Use 35 as the denominator.

hint: Use 35 as the common denominator.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\frac{10}{35} + \frac{7}{35} = \frac{17}{35}$.

## Simplified explanation

Change them to 35ths: 10 and 7. They add to 17.

body: The product of three numbers is 1197. Two of the numbers are 3 and 19. Find the third number.
hint: Multiply 3 by 19, then divide.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\frac{1197}{3 \times 19} = \frac{1197}{57} = 21$.

## Simplified explanation

$3 \times 19 = 57$. Then $1197 \div 57 = 21$.

body: Find the G.C.F. (H.C.F.) of $2^3 \times 3^2$ and $2^3 \times 3^4$.
hint: The HCF uses the lowest power of each prime.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The minimum exponents are 3 for 2 and 2 for 3, so the HCF is $2^3 \times 3^2 = 72$.

## Simplified explanation

Choose the smaller power of each number: $2^3$ and $3^2$. Then $8 \times 9 = 72$.

body:
Use the diagram, in which the two sloping sides of the triangle are equal and the arrowed lines are parallel, to answer the question.

Find the value of $a^\circ$.

media.caption: Isosceles triangle on a straight line. The left exterior angle is a°, the right interior angle is 56° and the apex angle is b°. An arrowed line from the apex makes 75° with the right side. A parallel line from the right corner makes 19° with the base, and c° is beside it.

hint: The triangle is isosceles, so the left base angle is also 56°.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The base angles are equal at $56^\circ$, so $a = 180^\circ - 56^\circ = 124^\circ$.

## Simplified explanation

The two equal sides make the left inside angle 56°. Angle $a$ is next to it on the straight line, so $a = 180 - 56 = 124$.

body:
Use the diagram, in which the two sloping sides of the triangle are equal and the arrowed lines are parallel, to answer the question.

What is the value of $b^\circ$?

media.caption: Isosceles triangle on a straight line. The left exterior angle is a°, the right interior angle is 56° and the apex angle is b°. An arrowed line from the apex makes 75° with the right side. A parallel line from the right corner makes 19° with the base, and c° is beside it.

options.hint: This is the sum of the two base angles.

hint: Both base angles of the triangle are 56°.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$b = 180^\circ - 2(56^\circ) = 68^\circ$.

## Simplified explanation

The base angles are 56° each, which makes 112°. The rest of the 180° is 68°.

body:
Use the diagram, in which the two sloping sides of the triangle are equal and the arrowed lines are parallel, to answer the question.

What is the value of $c^\circ$?

media.caption: Isosceles triangle on a straight line. The left exterior angle is a°, the right interior angle is 56° and the apex angle is b°. An arrowed line from the apex makes 75° with the right side. A parallel line from the right corner makes 19° with the base, and c° is beside it.

options.hint: This is a given angle. $c$ and 75° are co-interior.
The angles on the straight line add to 180°.

hint: The angles at the right base corner lie on a straight line.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$56 + c + 19 = 180$, so $c = 105$. Also, $c + 75 = 180$ as co-interior angles.

## Simplified explanation

The three angles at the corner make a straight line. So $c = 180 - 56 - 19 = 105$.

body: Simplify: $2ab^2 \times 3a^2b$

options.hint: Multiply the numbers and add the powers.
Correct. Multiply the numbers and add the powers.

hint: Multiply the numbers, then add the powers of each letter.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$2 \times 3 = 6$, $a^{1 + 2} = a^3$ and $b^{2 + 1} = b^3$.

## Simplified explanation

The numbers give 6. For $a$, the powers $1 + 2$ make 3. For $b$, the powers $2 + 1$ make 3.

body: In the relation $v = u + at$, find $v$ when $u = 6$, $a = 10$ and $t = 2$.
hint: Multiply $a$ by $t$ first.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$v = 6 + 10(2) = 26$.

## Simplified explanation

$10 \times 2 = 20$. Then $6 + 20 = 26$.

body:
The marks obtained by 10 children in a mental drill are 0, 1, 3, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 9, 9.

What is the modal mark?
hint: The mode is the most frequent mark.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The mark 9 has the highest frequency, 3.

## Simplified explanation

9 appears the most, three times.

body:
The marks obtained by 10 children in a mental drill are 0, 1, 3, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 9, 9.

Find the median mark.

options.hint: This is the 5th mark. Use the 5th and 6th marks.
This is the 6th mark. Use the 5th and 6th marks.

hint: With 10 marks, use the two middle ones.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The median is the mean of the 5th and 6th values: $\frac{5 + 7}{2} = 6$.

## Simplified explanation

The two middle marks are 5 and 7, and halfway between them is 6.

body:
The marks obtained by 10 children in a mental drill are 0, 1, 3, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 9, 9.

Calculate the mean mark.

options.hint: This is the number of children.
This is the total. Divide by 10.

hint: Add all the marks and divide by 10.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\frac{54}{10} = 5.4$.

## Simplified explanation

The ten marks add to 54. Then $54 \div 10 = 5.4$.

body:
The marks obtained by 10 children in a mental drill are 0, 1, 3, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 9, 9.

What is the probability that a child chosen at random scored 3 marks?

options.hint: Use the number of children, 10, as the denominator.
Use the number of children, 10, as the denominator.

hint: Count how many children scored 3.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$P(3) = \frac{2}{10}$.

## Simplified explanation

2 of the 10 children scored 3 marks.

body: A trader received a commission of $12\dfrac{1}{2}\%$ on sales made in a month. His commission was ₵35,000.00. Find his total sales for the month.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\frac{1}{8}S = 35{,}000$, so $S = 280{,}000$.

## Simplified explanation

The commission is one eighth of the sales. So the sales are $8 \times 35{,}000 = 280{,}000$.

body: A map of a large town is drawn to the scale of $1 : 100{,}000$. What is the distance in kilometres (km) represented by a line segment 4 cm long on the map?

options.hint: 1 cm on the map is 1 km.
1 cm on the map is 1 km.
1 cm on the map is 1 km.

hint: Change 100,000 cm to kilometres.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$4 \times 100{,}000 = 400{,}000$ cm, which is 4 km.

## Simplified explanation

100,000 cm is exactly 1 km. So each map centimetre stands for 1 km, and 4 cm stands for 4 km.

body: Adjoa and Ama share ₵600.00 between them in the ratio $3 : 2$. Find Adjoa's share.

options.hint: One part is ₵120.00, and Adjoa has 3 parts.
This is half of the amount.

hint: The ratio has 5 parts.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\frac{3}{5} \times 600 = 360$.

## Simplified explanation

5 parts make ₵600, so 1 part is ₵120. Adjoa gets 3 parts, which is ₵360.

body: Simplify: $\dfrac{2a}{3} - \dfrac{a - b}{2}$

options.hint: The minus sign changes $-b$ to $+b$ when the bracket opens.

hint: Use 6 as the common denominator, and be careful with the minus sign.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\frac{4a - 3(a - b)}{6} = \frac{4a - 3a + 3b}{6} = \frac{a + 3b}{6}$.

## Simplified explanation

Over 6 the top is $4a - 3(a - b)$. Opening the bracket gives $4a - 3a + 3b$, which is $a + 3b$.

body: $a^6 \div a^4 = 64$. Find $a$.
hint: Subtract the powers first.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$a^{6 - 4} = a^2 = 64$, so $a = \pm 8$, and 8 is the value among the options.

## Simplified explanation

Taking the powers away leaves $a^2 = 64$. And $8 \times 8 = 64$.

body: Find one-hundredth of 1.0756.

options.hint: The point moves 2 places to the left.

hint: Divide by 100.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$1.0756 \div 100 = 0.010756$.

## Simplified explanation

Dividing by 100 moves the point 2 places to the left.

body: What is the rule for this mapping?
hint: $y$ goes up by 2 each time.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The constant difference is 2, so $y = 2x + c$. With $(1, 1)$, $c = -1$.

## Simplified explanation

Each step adds 2, so the rule has $2x$. When $x = 1$, $2x$ is 2, and 1 less makes 1.

body: The circumference of a circular track is 440 m. Find the diameter of this track. $\left[\text{Take } \pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\right]$
hint: Circumference $= \pi d$.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$d = \frac{C}{\pi} = 440 \times \frac{7}{22} = 140$ m.

## Simplified explanation

$440 \div 22 = 20$, and $20 \times 7 = 140$.

body: If $r = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $s = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$, calculate $6(r + 2s)$.

options.hint: This is the bracket. Multiply it by 6.
This adds $r$ and $s$, and it leaves out the 6.

hint: Work out the bracket first.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$r + 2s = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$, and $6\begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -6 \\ 18 \end{pmatrix}$.

## Simplified explanation

Doubling $s$ gives $-4$ and 2. Adding $r$ gives $-1$ and 3. Multiplying by 6 gives $-6$ and 18.

body: Which of the following would you use to measure an angle?

options.hint: A set square draws set angles.
Correct. A protractor is marked in degrees.

hint: Which instrument is marked in degrees?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

A protractor has a scale in degrees for measuring angles.

## Simplified explanation

A protractor has degrees marked around its edge.

body: Express the ratio of 64 cm to 48 cm in simplest form.

options.hint: This is the wrong way round.
This is the wrong way round, and it can be reduced.

hint: Divide both numbers by their HCF.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The HCF of 64 and 48 is 16, so $64 : 48 = 4 : 3$.

## Simplified explanation

16 goes into both numbers. Dividing gives 4 and 3.

body:
In the diagram, $P \to P'$, $Q \to Q'$ and $R \to R'$. $PQR \to P'Q'R'$ is an enlargement.

What is the scale factor of the enlargement?

media.caption: Enlargement from O along two lines. Triangle PQR has PQ 3 m and RQ 2 m. Triangle P'Q'R' has P'Q' 1.5 m and R'Q' 1 m.

options.hint: The image is on the same side of $O$, and it is smaller.
The image is on the same side of $O$, so the factor is positive.
This goes from the image back to the object.

hint: Scale factor $=$ image length $\div$ object length.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$k = \frac{|P'Q'|}{|PQ|} = \frac{1.5}{3} = \frac{1}{2}$.

## Simplified explanation

3 m became 1.5 m, so the lengths are halved. The scale factor is $\frac{1}{2}$.

body:
In the diagram, $P \to P'$, $Q \to Q'$ and $R \to R'$. $PQR \to P'Q'R'$ is an enlargement.

If $|PR| = 3.6$ m, what is the length of $P'R'$?

media.caption: Enlargement from O along two lines. Triangle PQR has PQ 3 m and RQ 2 m. Triangle P'Q'R' has P'Q' 1.5 m and R'Q' 1 m.

hint: Multiply by the scale factor.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$|P'R'| = \frac{1}{2} \times 3.6 = 1.8$ m.

## Simplified explanation

The scale factor is $\frac{1}{2}$, so half of 3.6 m is 1.8 m.

body: Find the tangent of the angle marked $y$ in the diagram.

media.caption: Right-angled triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and hypotenuse 10 cm. Angle y is between the 6 cm side and the hypotenuse.

hint: $\tan$ is opposite over adjacent.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\tan y = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3}$.

## Simplified explanation

From angle $y$, the side across is 8 cm and the side next to it is 6 cm. $\frac{8}{6}$ reduces to $\frac{4}{3}$.

body: Kofi paid ₵270,000.00 for a TV set after he had been given a discount of 10%. Find the marked price.

options.hint: This adds 10% of what he paid. The 10% is of the marked price.
The marked price is higher than what he paid.

hint: He paid 90% of the marked price.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$0.9M = 270{,}000$, so $M = 300{,}000$.

## Simplified explanation

₵270,000 is 90% of the price, so 10% is ₵30,000 and 100% is ₵300,000.

body:
In a secondary school class, 23 pupils study Economics, 6 pupils study both Government and Economics, and 48 pupils study either Government or Economics or both.

What is the total number of pupils who study Government?

options.hint: This is the number who study only Economics.
This is the number who study Economics.
Those who study only Government number 25.

hint: Use $n(G \cup E) = n(G) + n(E) - n(G \cap E)$.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$48 = n(G) + 23 - 6$, so $n(G) = 31$.

## Simplified explanation

48 pupils in all take at least one subject, and 23 take Economics. So 25 take only Government. With the 6 who take both, that is 31.

body:
In a secondary school class, 23 pupils study Economics, 6 pupils study both Government and Economics, and 48 pupils study either Government or Economics or both.

How many pupils study only Government?

options.hint: This is the number who study only Economics.
This is the number who study Economics.

hint: Take the Economics pupils from the total.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$n(G \text{ only}) = 48 - 23 = 25$.

## Simplified explanation

Everyone who does not take Economics takes only Government. So $48 - 23 = 25$.

body:
In a secondary school class, 23 pupils study Economics, 6 pupils study both Government and Economics, and 48 pupils study either Government or Economics or both.

How many pupils study only Economics?

options.hint: This includes those who study both.
This is the number who study only Government.

hint: Take those who study both from the Economics pupils.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$n(E \text{ only}) = 23 - 6 = 17$.

## Simplified explanation

23 take Economics, and 6 of them also take Government. So 17 take only Economics.

body: When a certain number is subtracted from 10 and the result is multiplied by 2, the final result is 4. Find the number.
hint: Let the number be $n$ and write an equation.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$2(10 - n) = 4$, so $10 - n = 2$ and $n = 8$.

## Simplified explanation

Work backwards. $4 \div 2 = 2$, and $10 - 2 = 8$.

body: From the diagram, calculate the bearing of point $X$ from point $Y$.

media.caption: Compass lines at Y. The line to X points down and to the left, making 45° with the south line.

options.hint: Bearings are measured clockwise from north.
The 45° is measured from south, not north.

hint: Bearings are measured clockwise from north.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$X$ is $45^\circ$ past south, so the bearing is $180^\circ + 45^\circ = 225^\circ$.

## Simplified explanation

Clockwise from north to south is 180°. $X$ is another 45° past south, which makes 225°.

body: If 22% of the length of a rope is 55 cm, find the full length of the rope.

options.hint: This takes 22% of 55. The 55 cm is itself 22%.
The full length is longer than 55 cm.

hint: 55 cm is 22%. Find 100%.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\frac{55}{0.22} = 250$ cm.

## Simplified explanation

22% is 55 cm, so 2% is 5 cm. Then 100% is $50 \times 5 = 250$ cm.

body: Which of the following best describes the given construction?

media.caption: A horizontal line with two arcs marking it. A vertical line passes through the point P above the line and through crossing arcs below it.

options.hint: The construction starts from the point $P$, not the ends of the line.

options.text: Constructing the bisector of a line segment.
options.hint: The construction starts from the point $P$, not the ends of the line.

options.text: Constructing the perpendicular to a line.
options.hint: This is true, but the next statement is more exact.

options.text: Constructing a perpendicular to a given line from a point outside the line.

hint: Where is the point $P$ compared with the line?
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Arcs from $P$ cut the line at two points. Arcs from those points cross below the line, which gives the perpendicular from $P$.

## Simplified explanation

An arc from $P$ marks two points on the line. Arcs from those points cross on the other side, and joining to $P$ gives a right angle with the line.

hint: 1 is not prime, and 2 is the only even prime.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Every prime except 2 is odd, so $X \cap Y$ is $X$ without the 2.

## Simplified explanation

List the primes below 13, then the odd numbers below 13. Numbers on both lists form the intersection. Putting the lists together gives the union.

body: Three school children share some oranges as follows: Akwasi gets $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the total, and the remainder is shared between Abena and Jantuah in the ratio $3 : 2$. If Jantuah gets 24 oranges, how many does Akwasi get?
answer:
Jantuah's 2 parts are 24, so 1 part is 12.

Remainder: $5 \times 12 = 60$ oranges

This remainder is $\frac{2}{3}$ of the total, so Akwasi's $\frac{1}{3}$ is half of it:

$$\frac{60}{2} = 30$$

> [!answer]
> {{green:30}}
hint: Use Jantuah's share to find the remainder first.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The total is $\frac{3}{2} \times 60 = 90$ oranges, and $\frac{1}{3}$ of 90 is 30.

## Simplified explanation

24 oranges is 2 parts, so the 5 parts make 60. That is two thirds of all the oranges, so one third is 30.

body:
Using a ruler and a pair of compasses only,

(a) construct a triangle $XYZ$ in which $|YZ| = 6$ cm, angle $YZX = 60^\circ$ and $|ZX| = 9$ cm. Measure $|XY|$.

(b)(i) Construct the mediator of $XY$.

(b)(ii) Draw a circle with centre $X$ and a radius of 5 cm. Measure $|YA|$, where $A$ is the point of intersection of the mediator and the circle in the triangular region $XYZ$.

Type your measurements.
answer:
Draw $|YZ| = 6$ cm. Construct $60^\circ$ at $Z$ and mark $X$ on this arm so that $|ZX| = 9$ cm. Join $X$ to $Y$.

Bisect $XY$, and draw the circle with centre $X$ and radius 5 cm to cut the mediator at $A$.

> [!answer]
> {{green:$|XY| \approx 7.9$ cm and $|YA| = 5$ cm}}
hint: Any point on the mediator of $XY$ is the same distance from $X$ and $Y$.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The cosine rule gives $|XY|^2 = 36 + 81 - 54 = 63$, so $|XY| \approx 7.94$ cm. $A$ is on the mediator, so $|YA| = |XA| = 5$ cm.

## Simplified explanation

Build the triangle from the two sides and the 60° angle between them. $XY$ measures about 7.9 cm. $A$ is on the mediator, so it is as far from $Y$ as from $X$, which is 5 cm.

body: Solve the equation $\dfrac{2x - 1}{3} - \dfrac{x - 2}{4} = 1$
hint: The LCM of 3 and 4 is 12.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Check with $x = 2$: $\frac{3}{3} - \frac{0}{4} = 1$.

## Simplified explanation

Multiplying by 12 clears the fractions. Opening the brackets gives $5x + 2 = 12$. So $5x = 10$ and $x = 2$.

body: Factorise completely $2ap + aq - bq - 2bp$
hint: Group the first two terms and the last two terms.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Factorisation by grouping works because both groups share the factor $(2p + q)$.

## Simplified explanation

Take $a$ out of the first pair and $-b$ out of the second. Both leave $(2p + q)$.

hint: Be careful with the negative value of $m$.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$(-2)^2$ is positive, and subtracting $\frac{3}{-2}$ adds $\frac{3}{2}$.

## Simplified explanation

For (i), 4 times $-\frac{1}{4}$ is $-1$. For (ii), $\frac{3}{4}$ squared is $\frac{9}{16}$. Taking away $-\frac{3}{2}$ adds $\frac{24}{16}$, which gives $\frac{33}{16}$.

body:
The following table shows the distribution of voters in an election for class prefect.

| Candidate | Number of votes |
|---|---|
| Acquaye | 6 |
| Borquaye | 12 |
| Commey | 18 |

(i) Calculate the angle of each sector of a pie chart that illustrates the information.

(ii) What fraction of the votes was cast for Borquaye?
answer:
**(i)** Total votes: $6 + 12 + 18 = 36$, so each vote takes $360^\circ \div 36 = 10^\circ$.

Acquaye $60^\circ$, Borquaye $120^\circ$, Commey $180^\circ$

**(ii)** $\frac{12}{36} = \frac{1}{3}$

> [!answer]
> **(i)** {{green:Acquaye 60°, Borquaye 120°, Commey 180°}}  **(ii)** {{green:$\frac{1}{3}$}}
hint: Add the votes, then find the angle for one vote.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Sector angle $= \frac{f}{36} \times 360^\circ = 10f$ degrees. The angles add to $360^\circ$, which checks the working.

## Simplified explanation

There are 36 votes and 360° in a circle, so each vote is 10°. Multiply each number by 10. Borquaye has 12 of the 36 votes, which is a third.

body:
The heights in centimetres of 10 school children are as follows:

165, 165, 155, 159, 174

154, 169, 155, 155, 150

(i) Make a frequency table for the data.

(ii) Use your table to find the mode and the median of the distribution.
answer:
**(i)**

| Height (cm) | 150 | 154 | 155 | 159 | 165 | 169 | 174 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 1 | 1 | 3 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 |

**(ii)** Mode: 155, which has the highest frequency.

Median: the 5th and 6th values are 155 and 159, so

$$\frac{155 + 159}{2} = 157$$

> [!answer]
> **(ii)** {{green:mode 155 cm, median 157 cm}}
hint: With 10 values, the median uses the two middle ones.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The cumulative frequencies are 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10, which place the 5th and 6th values at 155 and 159.

## Simplified explanation

Count each height. 155 appears most, so it is the mode. In order, the two middle heights are 155 and 159, and halfway between them is 157.
